phrases.text: Measure S asks the voters of this community services district whether to repeal the special tax for police that its voters approved in 1997.
Measure S is a citizens' initiative, placed on the ballot by a petition signed by at least 10 percent of the district's registered voters.
The board then ordered it put to the voters without changes.
Since 1997, an annual special tax has helped pay for the salaries and benefits of the district's police and dispatch staff.
Measure S would repeal the 1997 police tax in full.
The measure's own title says the repeal would pave a path for an updated and modernized special tax measure.
Measure S needs a majority of the vote to pass.
The impartial analysis does not include a cost estimate for the measure.
Opponents say the district's budgets are audited every year, and repeal means lost revenue each year, forcing added cuts to police service.
Supporters say the 1997 tax has no citizen oversight or audits, and repeal lets voters decide on one single new police tax.
A yes vote repeals the 1997 special tax for police and dispatch staff.
A no vote leaves the 1997 special tax in place.
